I think you appreciate the endnotes more the second time around. I didn't give a fuck about the list of Jim Incandenza's works the first time I read it but it becomes more interesting when you know the full picture.

Anyway, here's my advice regarding the book:

  • The endnotes are just as much a part of the story as the regular chapters. Read all of them. The book is deliberately structured to weave in and out of the endnotes.

  • Some people treat the novel like a giant enigma that needs unwrapping but I don't think this is really true. There's a couple motifs you see like the Boston area being a giant body (with the individual settings of the story as parts), circular/annular things, and the allusions to Hamlet. That doesn't mean you need to keep detailed notes on these things. However, it is worth keeping track of the Canadian/Quebecois separatist groups as they are a big part of the plot.

  • Once you reach the end, read the first chapter again. I would call it the "end" of the book (it is structured to be annular, hence why you see that word so much) and it will wrap up the book better than the last chapter.
